text:
anna: quick heads-up — ran a focused profile this morning on the structured-output/chat-route with tool/function calling enabled. staging w/ kv-cache-on, continuous-batcher default policies. results below.

kai: nice, what stood out?

anna: two big things: (1) the decode loop spends a lot longer when a tool pause is expected (stop-token detection + handoff), and (2) KV cache churn when we pause/flush causes extra kernel churn + memcpy. p95 latency +13% vs no-tools.

sarah: do you have numbers?

anna: pasted raw sampling from the runtime profiler (single 8xA100 equivalent host):
```
PROFILE SAMPLE (chat-route/tool-call)
- baseline decode step (no tool): 0.85ms/step
- when stop-token matched and tool invoked: 11.5ms latency gap (awaiting tool ack/handler)
- KV cache serialize/evict spike: +2.2ms per pause during resume
- kernel rebind (small sequence len change): +0.9ms per resume
- batching efficiency drop: effective batch size down from 28->9 for tool-waiting queues
```

mike: ouch — so it's both waiting for the tool and also losing batching efficiency and causing extra memcpy.

anna: exactly. I instrumented the queue buckets: we currently keep tool-waiting requests in the same high-priority queue. That lets them cut in front of long tokens, but it also starves steady decode batches and prevents the continuous-batcher from forming large batches.

kai: hypothesis: we should separate "tool-await" bucket and treat them as low-priority for batch formation, but still allow opportunistic coalescing when many tool-waits line up. Also cap token_budget for those buckets to avoid huge KV churn.

anna: prototype config I tried:
```json
{
  "queue_policies": {
    "default": {"priority": 10, "token_budget": 1024},
    "tool_await": {"priority": 2, "token_budget": 64, "prefer_short": true, "opportunistic_coalesce_ms": 25}
  }
}
```

sarah: why token_budget 64? seems low.

anna: picked small to avoid long-running tokens holding KV in memory as they wait. The idea: resume small slices fast, keep kv working set small so kernel selection remains stable (no rebinds).

mike: did you try lowering opport_coalesce? 25ms might still block.

anna: tried 0/5/25/50. 0 or 5ms prevented any meaningful coalescing and p95 stayed high due to lack of batching. 25ms was sweet spot in our trace where occasional tool-wait alignments created batches of 4-8 and improved throughput w/o hurting tail too much.

kai: what about kernel selection? we saw rebinds when sequence lengths change after resume, right?

anna: yes — rebinds occur if the runtime switches kernel path due to sequence length or quantization fallback when KV get serialized. Workaround: keep kernel affinity stable for the slot for N ms after a pause (sticky-kernel-window). I experimented with sticky-kernel-window = 150ms and it reduced rebinds by ~60%.

sarah: any regressions to be worried about? perf-bot flagged a regression earlier, right?

perf-bot: regression-alert: chat-route (tool-enabled) p95 +12.8% (compare baseline: 2026-11-02) — correlated with deploy 2026-11-14 03:12 UTC. See run: https://perf.redwood/reports/4782

mike: so action items?

anna: proposed immediate experiments (short term):
- split queue: tool-await low-priority with token_budget=64 and prefer_short=true
- opportunistic_coalesce_ms=25 for tool-await only
- sticky-kernel-window=150ms to avoid kernel rebind churn on resume
- small KV serialization debounce: delay full kv-serialize until after first resumed chunk completes (avoid double-serialize)

kai: sounds good. For rollout, prefer canary on one dedicated host pool and a/b p95 monitoring. Also add a metric: "tool-await-batch-size" and "kv-serialize-count".

sarah: agree. Also add an opt-in flag on Dedicated customers to keep previous behavior until we're confident.

mike: checkpoint: I'll wire the queue policy change + metrics. anna, can you push the sticky-kernel-window and debounce in runtime branch? then I'll canary.

anna: yep — PR incoming later today. rough patch notes in PR:
- add queue policy type: tool_await
- token_budget tuning example
- sticky kernel window config
- kv serialize debounce hook

kai: any thoughts on changing stop-token handling itself? e.g., pre-scan tokens to detect likely tool calls to avoid starting large batches that will be interrupted.

anna: good idea — lightweight prefix classifier could label requests "likely-tool" at enqueue time and route accordingly. cheap n-gram classifier or rule-based detection. I did a quick run: classifier with 92% precision reduced mid-batch interrupts by ~70%. Implementation risk is low.

sarah: add that as low-effort follow-up. tracker: INC-RT-2026-41.

perf-bot: canary results pending — will post when 2h window completes.

mike: thanks — let's sync tomorrow after canary. :thumbsup:

anna: TL;DR: tool pauses cause batching losses + kv/kernel churn. short-term mitigations (queue split, token_budget cap, sticky kernel window) look promising; classifier + debounce are follow-ups.
